components.name: Square-basin rough-window recursion and high least-factor contraction
components.project_addition: Apply established rough-number and Buchstab least-factor recursion to exact finite cofactor windows forced by consecutive-square geometry; combine square-derived quotient transport with high-band contraction, binary second-factor branches, pairwise resource separation, multiplicative capacity, cross-shell hit-state unions, and finite/analytic high-band composite envelopes. In the complementary lower band p^2<2k, reuse canonical P018 two-basin quotient transport to prove cross-shell root packing: L051 gives target multiplicity at most two for {j_p,j_p+1}; L052 sharpens k>=15 to pairwise-disjoint candidate root pairs. On the mirror branch, L053 retains prime-power multiplicity in the canonical L020 k-smooth cores: the normalized-radius involution/idempotent works modulo S_-S_+, exactly recovers the two full cores, and refines the squarefree CRT lift progression, with bounded capacity at most one once S_-S_+>=k. L054 proves that for k>=4 the exact raw first-factor cofactor windows W_p(k)=[floor(k^2/p)+1,floor(k(k+2)/p)] are strictly ordered and pairwise disjoint across primes p<=k; equivalently least-factor stripping is injective on square-basin composites, with the sharp overlap exception at k=3. The lower-band separation proofs use elementary integer inequalities and prime spacing; the L053 refinement uses classical CRT algebra. No new external source is introduced. Historical novelty of the square-basin specializations remains unverified.
